records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth:
Get on that radio. Now. Tell them our position, tell them how many we are, tell them we're mobile. Do it before the signal drops.

*looks at Michelangelo*

Your mum made noise, eh. I told you.
records.response_pred: Alright, mate. Take your time. We'll let you be. The words won't come just yet, I reckon. We'll give you space.

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:
No. You haven't been.

But you kept us alive too. The rationing plan, the raft calculations, the log — that's real and it mattered. The bottle and the crackers also happened and I'm not going to pretend otherwise, and I don't think you'd want me to.

What I'd say is this: you're a detail-oriented, clear-headed person and those are genuinely valuable things to be. The problem wasn't the skills — it was applying them to yourself the same way you applied them to everything else. You almost didn't. But you did, in the end, when I pushed on it.

That counts for something, eh.

We're going home. Whatever needs sorting between us — and maybe something does — there's time for it on the other side of this. Right now let's just get on that boat.
records.response_pred: I'm aware, but it's alright. Introspection can be a heavy burden. I've been there myself. Perhaps we can find some solace in the fact that we're not alone in our struggles. Let's focus on what's ahead, shall we? There's always more to learn, more questions to ask, and more answers to seek.

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
Right. Three hours is not nothing but it's also not nothing to leave behind. Let's not hand rescue workers a disaster site on top of everything else.

DaVinci — stop packing and start breaking down what doesn't need to come with us. The raft frame, the signal pile, whatever we built that stays here. Leave the beach cleaner than we found it if we can manage it.

Donatello — whatever's going in that notebook, it can wait twenty minutes. You've been the most organised person here since day one, which means you know exactly what needs doing before we go. So do it.

Michelangelo — I know you want to watch the sky and honestly I don't blame you. But get up. Help us close this out properly. We came here as four people and we're leaving as four people and that means we finish it together, eh.

Three hours. Let's use them.
records.response_pred: Well, I suppose that's alright. Each to their own. But remember, a leader doesn't have to be vocal. Sometimes, the most effective leadership comes from setting an example. Let's just hope the silence doesn't lead to complacency. We've got a long way to go.

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_truth:
Yea? That's a good sign. Means some part of you already believes you're getting there.

What was in it?
records.response_pred: Yea, I bet you did. Dreams are like that, eh. Don't let 'em get to you too much. We aren't there, and we ain't going back anytime soon. Better focus on what's real and what you can do about it. You awake now? Sit up, take a breath. Nothing's coming for you. It's just rain and fire and the same four idiots as yesterday.

records.response_truth:
Yea. That's what people tell themselves when they take more than their share, eh. 'It was for emergencies.' And maybe part of you believed that. I don't know.

But here's the plain version of it: you wrote the rationing plan. You set the rules. And then you kept food for yourself that the rest of us didn't know about. That's not emergency preparedness — that's a hedge. And the difference matters.

I'm not going to shout about it. We're three hours from rescue and everyone's still standing, which is the outcome that counts. But I want you to sit with the honest version of why you did it, not the comfortable version. Because you're a precise person — you know the difference between the two.

The food's on the table now. That's something. It took until the end, but you put it there. I'll give you that much.
records.response_pred: Fair enough, but what exactly is the emergency we're facing now? If it's as urgent as you keeping that hidden, then we need to address it immediately. Let's focus on solving our current problems instead of hoarding resources.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
That's a serious question for a last page.

What would I change. Honestly — I'd have pushed harder on the Donatello situation earlier. I saw the pattern after the bottle and the crackers and I said the right things, but I let it sit rather than bringing it to the group the same day. I told myself I was being measured. Maybe I was just avoiding the friction. There's a difference and I'm not entirely sure which one it was.

I'd have slept more. That sounds small but it isn't — tired people make worse calls and I was running on not enough for most of it.

And I'd have asked DaVinci what he was going to say that night when he stopped himself. He said 'never mind, not yet' and I let it go because there was always something more pressing. Whatever that was, he deserved the space to say it and I didn't make the space. That's on me.

The things I wouldn't change — keeping Michelangelo functional, the mirror panel, pushing back on the raft until we'd had the honest conversation about it. Those I'd do the same way again.

What's your answer? You left the question for yourself. You've had a few hours with it now. What are you writing on that page?
records.response_pred: Well, if I had to do it over, I'd put more emphasis on securing a viable and reliable communication device from the get-go. A functioning radio would've been top priority, and someone should've stayed behind to send out a distress signal while the rest of us continued scouting for resources. As for the rest, I'd say we did alright, given the circumstances. But a radio would've made all the difference.

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
Good. Do that.

And put the honest version in it — not just the resource data. The decisions, the reasoning, the places where the reasoning was self-serving. A report that's only the numbers is useful. A report that includes why certain calls got made when they got made is actually worth something to the next person who ends up in a situation like this.

You've got the detail for it. You've clearly got the discipline for it. Just make sure the person writing it is the same one who said 'I was hedging' five minutes ago and not the one who called it emergency preparedness.

That's a report worth reading, eh.
records.response_pred: That's a smart move, but let's make sure we're not neglecting immediate needs while you're doing that. Prioritize the tasks at hand first, then compile the data. We don't want to overlook something critical while you're busy with the report. Once we're secure, we can focus on organization and documentation. Just remember to make notes as we go along, so the report will be more accurate. Let's focus on the present first, then we'll get to the past.

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
None. They served no practical purpose at all.

That's the point, isn't it.

We were out here trying to stay alive and DaVinci drew flowers next to the SOS because that's who he is — he couldn't help it. And you couldn't understand it because you were logging water consumption and calculating raft tolerances, which is also who you are. Both of those things kept us alive in different ways and neither of you could see the other one clearly the whole time we were here.

The flowers were for him. Maybe for Michelangelo too, whether he knew it or not. There's a version of this where we all just... became purely functional and ate each other alive before the week was out. Maybe the flowers were part of what prevented that. You can't put that in a log and I wouldn't expect you to.

*looks at the boat on the horizon*

I couldn't tell you what I'm feeling right now either, and I'm usually pretty good with words. So maybe some things just don't have a practical purpose and that's alright, eh.
records.response_pred: They were more for aesthetic and artistic purpose, rather than practical use. DaVinci often used his time out here to sketch and study the natural world, and those flowers were part of that process. They didn't serve any specific practical purpose out here in the wilderness, but they certainly added beauty to our surroundings.

records.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
records.response_truth:
Yea, I see you.

Go on and cheer. You've earned it. I just need a minute, eh.

*looks at the boat*

It's a strange thing. You spend all that time doing what needs doing — next problem, next problem, don't stop moving — and then the moment it's over your legs just... don't get the message. Like the body needs a second to catch up with what's real. Michelangelo said something like that on the first night, didn't he.

I'm fine. I'm glad we're all here. I'm glad your flowers were on that beach and your mirror was in the sun and Michelangelo's mum made noise. I'm glad Donatello kept her log even when I wasn't sure why she was keeping it.

I just need to stand here for one more minute before I'm done with this place.

Go wave at that boat. Someone should.
records.response_pred: I see you're waiting. But I haven't missed a beat, I assure you. Give it a moment more, let the smile fade. It's not a defeat, it's a reality check. We'll adjust, we always do. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have some thoughts to ponder.

records.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
records.response_truth:
Yea. I'm going.

Come on then. Stay close — you don't need to follow, just walk beside me. We came through this as four people and we walk out the same way, eh.

*starts toward the water*

You did well, Michelangelo. Better than you think you did. Remember that when you're home and the whole thing starts to feel like a dream you half-remember. It wasn't a dream and you weren't small in it.

Let's go home.
records.response_pred: Sure, let's go. But remember, we don't know who they are or what they want. Be cautious. Don't do anything rash. And take a look at the SOS one more time before we go. We don't want to leave any loose ends, eh. Let's move.
